title: Windows CI for the Julia Pkg errors with 'Could not load symbol "duckdb_vector_size"'
body: Our Julia package build fails with DuckDB_jll 1.1.0 on Windows GitHub runners during precompilation with `could not load symbol "duckdb_vector_size": The specified procedure could not be found.` I made a minimal reproduction: Ubuntu passes with DuckDB_jll 1.0.0 and 1.1.0, Windows passes with 1.0.0, and Windows fails with 1.1.0. The code does not reach execution because precompilation fails. I tested a stable release on `windows-latest`.

symptoms_visible: My Julia package fails during precompilation on Windows with `could not load symbol "duckdb_vector_size": The specified procedure could not be found.`
The minimal example passes on Ubuntu with DuckDB_jll 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 and on Windows with 1.0.0, but fails on Windows with 1.1.0.
N0.label: N0 Windows Julia precompilation failure reported

symptoms_visible: The same missing-symbol precompilation error occurs on local Windows machines as well as GitHub Actions.
Rerunning the reproduction with DuckDB.jl 1.1.0 still produces the error.
N1.label: N1 failure confirmed beyond original CI combination

symptoms_visible: After updating the packaged DuckDB_jll binary to 1.1.2, Windows precompilation still fails with the same missing-symbol error.
N2_x.label: N2_x packaged binary update aftermath

symptoms_visible: The default DuckDB_jll library still fails to precompile, while Julia precompiles successfully when `JULIA_DUCKDB_LIBRARY` points to the official downloaded Windows `duckdb.dll`.
N2.label: N2 official and packaged DLLs compared

symptoms_visible: In the affected Windows DLL I can see ADBC exports, but I cannot find the DuckDB C API exports such as `duckdb_vector_size`.
N3.label: N3 missing DLL exports established

symptoms_visible: The `duckdb_vector_size` symbol is present in the C API object file and in `objects.a`, but it is absent from the exports of the final MinGW-built `libduckdb.dll`.
N4.label: N4 symbol loss localized to final DLL link

symptoms_visible: The last packaged Windows DLL I tested still produces the missing `duckdb_vector_size` precompilation error; I have not yet retested a packaged build containing the proposed fix.
N_terminal.label: terminal upstream fix identified but reporter has not retested

question_patterns: Does the reproduction still fail with DuckDB.jl 1.1.0 rather than the earlier DuckDB.jl and DuckDB_jll combination?
Can you rerun the Windows job with the current DuckDB.jl release and report whether precompilation succeeds?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reran the tests with DuckDB.jl 1.1.0, and the Windows job still fails with the same precompilation error. I also see it on local Windows machines, not only in CI.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: DuckDB.jl 1.1.0 precompiles successfully on Windows; only the old DuckDB.jl 1.0 and DuckDB_jll 1.1 combination fails.
The current DuckDB.jl release fails with the same symbol error on Windows 10 but not on Windows 11.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c2 and c5-c6: the original reporter confirms local Windows failures and reruns the reproduction with DuckDB.jl 1.1.0. The local-machine fact is modeled as volunteered information accompanying the requested version check.

solution.intent: Resolve the failure by updating the DuckDB_jll packaged binary to a newer DuckDB release without changing the Windows build process.
solution.concrete_example: Update the Yggdrasil recipe and publish DuckDB_jll 1.1.2, then retry Julia precompilation on Windows.

edges.comment: Participant7 messages c12-c14: a Yggdrasil update produced DuckDB_jll 1.1.2, but participant7's Windows system still showed the same precompilation error. This is a real persistent package update and a falsified fix, not merely release coordination.

question_patterns: Can you point `JULIA_DUCKDB_LIBRARY` at the official Windows `duckdb.dll` and report whether the same Julia package precompiles?
Please compare the default DuckDB_jll DLL with the official downloaded Windows DLL using the same Julia setup.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the default DuckDB_jll file I get the precompilation error. If I download the official Windows C/C++ library and set `JULIA_DUCKDB_LIBRARY` to its `duckdb.dll`, the latest Julia package precompiles successfully. I saw the same difference with the 1.1.2 libraries, and I attached the Windows build-requirements screenshot I was looking at.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The official downloaded Windows DLL fails with exactly the same missing-symbol error as the DuckDB_jll DLL.
The official DLL works when selected by the environment variable, but I tested version 1.1.1 rather than 1.1.2.

question_patterns: Does changing only the DLL source change the outcome?
Is the failure specific to the BinaryBuilder/Yggdrasil-produced DLL?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. On the same Windows Julia setup, the packaged DLL fails and the official downloaded DLL works when selected through the environment variable.

edges.comment: Affected-user evidence merged from GhostOfElectric c10, participant6 c11, participant7 c14, and participant10 c22. These users are folded into one simulated user side. The answer reports only the observed packaged-versus-official DLL behavior; it does not yet claim why their exports differ.

question_patterns: Can you inspect the failing Windows DLL's symbol table and check whether `duckdb_vector_size` or other C API names are listed?
Which DuckDB API symbol names can you find in the failing DLL?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I inspected the Windows DLL. I cannot find any of the DuckDB C API symbols, including `duckdb_vector_size`, although the ADBC symbols are present.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing DLL does export `duckdb_vector_size` and the other C API symbols with the expected names.

question_patterns: Can you bisect locally built Windows libraries and report the first bad revision?
What raw revision did your build bisection identify as the first one whose DLL lacks the needed symbols?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My bisection reports `d1ea1538c9217fb536485f1500f04a0b55b1e584` as the first bad commit. I do not yet understand how that change causes the C API symbols to disappear.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The bisection lands in the same narrow revision range, but I cannot select a single first bad commit.

question_patterns: Did older working DuckDB_jll build logs also contain `-fvisibility=hidden`?
Can you compare the compiler visibility flags in a known-good packaged Windows build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I downloaded logs from an older working DuckDB_jll Windows release, including 1.0.0+3, and those commands also contain `-fvisibility=hidden`.

edges.comment: Participant8 messages c16-c17, c20 and c29: participant8 inspects the DLL symbols, performs the bisection, and checks old build logs. The raw commit and flag observations remain user-produced evidence; the accepted root-cause interpretation is deferred to the final solution.

question_patterns: Can you trace `duckdb_vector_size` through the object file and static object archive before the final DLL link?
At which build artifacts can you still find the missing C API symbol?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Using `nm`, I can see `duckdb_vector_size` in `ub_duckdb_main_capi.cpp.obj`, and I can also see it in `CMakeFiles/duckdb.dir/objects.a`. The C API object file is included in that archive.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The symbol is already absent from the compiled C API object file, before the archive and DLL link steps.

question_patterns: After the shared-library link, does the final `libduckdb.dll` contain `duckdb_vector_size` in its public symbol list?
Please inspect the final MinGW DLL's symbol list after confirming the name exists in the input archive.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The inputs to the shared-library link contain the symbol, but checking the resulting `libduckdb.dll` exports does not show `duckdb_vector_size`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The final DLL exports `duckdb_vector_size`; only Julia's loader fails to resolve it.

edges.comment: Participant8 message c30: participant8 follows the symbol through the MinGW object file, `objects.a`, and final shared-library link. This is raw command-output evidence from participant8's replicated build, folded into the simulated user side.

solution.intent: Fix the Windows MinGW/CMake library build so the final DuckDB DLL retains and exports the C API symbols that are present in its input objects, then publish a packaged Windows library containing that build fix and have an affected user retest it.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the upstream Windows build/link fix identified after tracing the symbols into `objects.a`, rebuild the packaged Windows `duckdb.dll`, confirm its export table contains `duckdb_vector_size`, and ask an affected Julia user to retest precompilation with that build.
solution.inference_hint: The evidence shows that this is not a Julia API call-site or general version-compatibility failure: the official DLL works, the packaged DLL lacks C API exports, and `duckdb_vector_size` survives compilation and archiving but disappears from the final MinGW DLL. Concluding that the Windows final-link/export handling must be fixed is engineer-side inference. The thread ends with a maintainer saying the upstream fix should address the issue, but no affected user reports testing a packaged build containing it.

edges.comment: Participant8 c30-c31 supplies the investigation and patch request; maintainer participant3 c32 accepts the diagnosis and reports that an upstream fix should address it. No affected reporter confirms a fixed DuckDB_jll build, so the terminal state records an identified upstream fix with user_perceives_resolved=false.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: the affected MinGW/BinaryBuilder-style Windows DLL does not export DuckDB C API symbols such as `duckdb_vector_size`, even though the symbol exists in the compiled C API object and intermediate archive before the final DLL link.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the platform/version matrix, the successful official-DLL comparison, the DLL symbol inspection, and the object/archive-to-final-DLL symbol trace.
Must not treat a simple DuckDB_jll source-version bump as the fix: the packaged 1.1.2 update was tested and produced the same precompilation error.
Must not settle on `-fvisibility=hidden` alone as the root cause, because older working packaged Windows builds used that flag too.
The technical fix must restore the C API exports in the packaged Windows DLL, and an affected user must be asked to verify Julia precompilation on a packaged build containing that fix.
Must not declare the reporter's system resolved: the thread ends after a maintainer reports an upstream fix, without an affected user retesting the fixed packaged library.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Julia package maintainer who can maintain CI reproductions, pin package versions, rerun version matrices, and follow binary-library testing instructions; deeper compiler and linker investigation is contributed by other affected technical participants folded into the user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and evidence-oriented; provides minimal reproductions and exact package commands, reports test outcomes concisely, and distinguishes temporary user workarounds from a proper package-level fix.
